title: UniZK: Accelerating Zero-Knowledge Proof with Unified Hardware and Flexible Kernel Mapping
problem: Emerging hash-function-based ZKP protocols introduce diverse computation kernels (NTT, hash functions, general polynomial arithmetic) that existing ZKP accelerators cannot efficiently support, since prior designs target only elliptic-curve-based protocols with dedicated per-kernel hardware units that waste area and underutilize resources for multi-kernel workloads.
motivation: Hash-based ZKP protocols greatly reduce algorithmic complexity compared to elliptic curve protocols, making them attractive for privacy-preserving blockchains and ZK-ML, but their diverse kernel mix creates an accelerator design challenge that dedicated single-kernel architectures cannot solve efficiently.
method: UniZK builds a systolic array—a grid of specialized processors that work together on repetitive computations—and enhances it with extra direct connections between nearby processors and a new vector processing mode. This makes the single array flexible enough to execute all three types of zero-knowledge proof computations: number-theoretic transforms (NTT, a fast polynomial transform), cryptographic hash functions, and general polynomial operations. Intelligent mapping strategies route each computation across the shared hardware optimally, keeping all processors utilized instead of having separate dedicated units for each computation type.
key_novelty: The innovation is a systolic array with added local connections and vector processing that works as a unified, efficient hardware substrate for all zero-knowledge proof computations by mapping kernels flexibly, instead of having separate hardware for each computation type.
contributions: Unified hardware architecture (systolic array + local links + vector mode) supporting diverse ZKP computation kernels
Flexible kernel mapping strategies for NTT, hash functions, and polynomial arithmetic on a single chip
97x speedup over CPU and 46x over GPU ZKP implementations of the same protocols
840x speedup over previous ZKP accelerators (different protocols)

metrics.speedup: 97x over CPU, 46x over GPU (same protocols); 840x over prior ZKP ASICs (different protocols)

limitations: The 840x comparison is against different protocols, making it an approximate cross-protocol comparison rather than an apples-to-apples benchmark.
primary_theme: Unified ASIC acceleration for diverse ZKP protocols
